data.body: RETRACTION of the previous entry's generalisation. The observation is sound and directly evidenced: 4329's close-review returned 'stale-code: 4 dependency file(s) changed' naming the files its own change landed - that is the gate reporting its own reason, not my inference. But the conclusions I drew from it - 'roughly doubling LLM spend per leaf' and 'throughput is now gated by the review/attestation cycle' - are UNTESTED extrapolations from a single observation, stated as fact. They do not meet this project's experimental standard and must not be acted on. Standing rule adopted for the rest of this run: any behaviour I classify as a BUG goes through /rebar-debug for a proven, cited root cause before I act on it or record it as established. Applied so far: a83f (sign fence) and de95 (order-dependent flake) were both handed to /rebar-debug rather than diagnosed by me. Not applicable to: correcting my own plan prose to match landed code, which is authoring, not diagnosis.
